(a) NotFoundError messages from multi_project_search._resolve_by_recency and symbol_source.source_with_items embed `[[next:search:<segment>]]`; server._run_tool re-raises MCPToolError unchanged and __main__ prints `Error: {exc}`, so the most common failure (bad target) is the only response whose follow-up is unrendered — and it leaks even when output.next_pointers.enabled=false. (b) build_session_start_context calls format_overview_card directly and never imports resolve_pointers/strip_pointers, so the turn-0 pack advertises `[[next:lookup-show:pkg.mod:context]]` tokens no client understands, while the same card served via get_overview renders `→ get_context(targets=[…])`. (1) Add `render_error_text(text: str, surface: str, *, pointers_enabled: bool) -> str` in application/envelope.py (resolve_pointers when enabled else strip_pointers). title: A `read` pointer action so indexed tools can hand off a ready-made read_file call (indexed → filesystem bridge)
problem: The pointer grammar has five actions (lookup | lookup-show | search | overview | why) and no way to render read_file or grep, so the indexed → filesystem direction exists only as prose. get_symbol(depth=source) over symbol_source.max_lines records a ledger entry with recovery="" and says `read <path> directly`, even though the chunk's source_path/start_line are known; get_why evidence locators (`docs/adr/0001.md:12-40`) are inert backticks; read_file's own continuation note is MCP syntax (`offset=`) on the CLI where the flag is --offset. The real corpus shows agents then hand-assemble loop-side Reads (31 Reads across 12 rollouts, 11 rejected for a wrong parameter name).
mechanism: Extend _POINTER_RE's action alternation with `read`, using the existing third group as the span: `[[next:read:<path>:<start>-<end>]]` (paths contain `/` and `.`, never `:` or `]`, so the grammar is safe; `_is_invalid_symbol_pointer` ignores the new action). Add `pointer_read(path, start, end)` beside pointer_token, and a `_render_read_pointer` branch: MCP → `→ read_file(file_path="{p}", offset={s}, limit={n})`, CLI → `→ pydocs-mcp read_file {p} --offset {s} --limit {n}`.
